profile.summary: The read classification part of Hall and Coin 2024: label each non-human read in a sputum-like metagenome as Mycobacterium tuberculosis or not. Kraken2 and minimap2 are each run with three databases, standard and custom, on simulated and artificial real Nanopore and Illumina data. It is for people building culture-free tuberculosis sequencing pipelines who need to choose a classifier and database, including on a laptop.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results, Classification of Mycobacterium reads

We benchmarked kraken and minimap2 for read classification, using 3 different databases for each tool. For kraken, we used the standard database (standard) and a version of the standard database that is capped at 8 GB (standard-8).

Such databases allow for execution on a laptop, without sacrificing accuracy, an especially important consideration in low-resource settings. We make all customized databases and pipelines freely available.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: How accurately each tool and database labels reads as M. tuberculosis, with as few false positives and false negatives as possible, and what it costs in runtime and memory. The authors frame this as a step toward sequencing directly from sputum, where contamination is higher than in culture.

quotes.text: We benchmarked kraken and minimap2 for read classification, using 3 different databases for each tool. For kraken, we used the standard database (standard) and a version of the standard database that is capped at 8 GB (standard-8).
We assess the performance of these configurations using sensitivity, specificity, Youden’s index, peak memory usage, and runtime (rate—reads per second).
WGS work is done from culture and therefore does not contain much contamination by design.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Simulated reads mimic sputum: 46% bacteria, 46% human, 6% M. tuberculosis complex and 1% each virus and NTM, 4.5 gigabases of Nanopore and 0.9 of Illumina. The artificial real set combines real reads from three 1000 Genomes people, an M. tuberculosis isolate and the ZymoBIOMICS HMW standard, so each read's true taxon is known. Classification uses the non-human reads left after host removal: 100,733 simulated Nanopore reads, 1,417,015 simulated Illumina pairs, 915,209 real Nanopore reads and 21,172,961 real Illumina pairs. Simulation genomes were kept out of the custom kraken Mycobacterium database.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Kraken2 uses the standard, standard-8 and a custom Mycobacterium database; minimap2 uses an M. tuberculosis database, the Clockwork decontamination database and a Mycobacterium genus database. A true positive is an M. tuberculosis read classified as M. tuberculosis. Each configuration is scored by sensitivity, specificity and Youden's index with Wilson score 95% intervals, plus mean runtime and peak memory over 10 runs with 4 threads.

We assess the performance of these configurations using sensitivity, specificity, Youden’s index, peak memory usage, and runtime (rate—reads per second).
All tools were run using 4 threads for consistency. Runtime and peak memory were calculated as the mean and maximum, respectively, from executing each method 10 times.

no_run_guide_reason: The README's example usage shows how to download the custom databases and classify one's own reads, not how to score classifications against the truth files. It says the Snakemake pipeline produces all results but gives no command or configuration steps for running it.

Human read removal (Tables 1 to 4) is out of the store's scope for this record but uses the same datasets.
